reason: The differentiation signals should guide the stem-cell population toward muscle precursors, the first stage described in the chapter.
expectation: A subset of the population will develop into muscle precursors.

effect: The signals produced myoblasts with muscle-related genes active; the next step is to join them into a multinucleated fibre.
reaction: The contrast between retained muscle proteins and secreted collagen is useful.
reason: The fusion proteins match the membranes of adjacent myoblasts, as described on the board.
expectation: The myoblasts will fuse into a muscle fibre with multiple nuclei.

effect: The myoblasts fused into a multinucleated fibre with actin–myosin machinery; its grip sites are still covered.
reaction: The one-cell outline makes the result of fusion clear.
reason: The calcium pulse is the available signal for activating the fibre's filaments.
expectation: Calcium will uncover actin's grip sites and allow the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites, allowing ATP-dependent myosin cycling and filament sliding; the fibre now needs to become ready again.
reaction: The distinction between sliding filaments and shortening filaments is clear.
reason: Calcium-pumping membranes should return calcium to storage so the fibre can relax.
expectation: ATP-powered pumps will remove calcium from around the filaments, allowing the fibre to relax and reset.

effect: Calcium pumping stopped the pull and reset the fibre; the next goal is to build and attach both muscles.
reaction: It is useful to see that relaxation also requires ATP and an outside pull for lengthening.
reason: The biceps sheaths have empty spaces for muscle fibres and tendon routes across the arm.
expectation: The fibres will fill the sheaths to form a biceps muscle with tendons.

effect: The fibre needed connective matrix first; the resulting fascicles provide bundles for both muscles.
reaction: The distinction between a fibre's membrane and its surrounding connective layer is helpful, though I missed that intermediate step.
reason: The biceps sheaths have spaces for the newly formed muscle bundles and tendon routes toward the shoulder and radius.
expectation: The fascicles will form a biceps muscle within the sheaths, with its tendons in place.

effect: The fascicles now form the two biceps heads, with connective tissue carrying force into the tendons.
reaction: The force-tracing inset connects the microscopic fibres to the tendon clearly.
reason: The fascicles transformed into biceps, so I need to check how the remaining triceps sheaths can be filled.
expectation: The compatibility list should show the next available ingredient for building the triceps.

effect: The inspection automatically used the remaining fascicles to build the triceps; both muscles are now ready for attachment.
reaction: The different head origins make the triceps anatomy more specific than I expected.
reason: The biceps tendons lead toward the shoulder and radius, so the movable arm skeleton is the natural attachment target.
expectation: The biceps tendons will attach to the skeleton across the elbow.

effect: The biceps is attached and shown flexing the elbow; the arm assembly still needs an extensor.
reaction: The two poses clarify how the biceps pulls on the radius.
reason: The triceps is the remaining muscle and should fill the extensor slot.
expectation: The triceps will attach across the elbow, completing the opposing muscle arrangement.

effect: The triceps filled the extensor slot, completing the arm and showing how opposite attachments turn similar pulls into flexion and extension.
reaction: The comparison of the two muscles' attachments makes their opposing actions clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Activating and resetting the fibre was most worthwhile: the planned diagrams distinguish sliding from filament shortening and show why relaxation also needs ATP.

leastWorthwhile.text: Checking the triceps compatibility was less interesting than the constructions themselves, although it usefully revealed and automatically performed the next operation.

surprise.text: I was surprised that relaxation involves ATP-powered calcium pumping and that an outside pull lengthens the fibre.

arbitrary.text: The need to add extracellular matrix before filling the biceps sheaths was not obvious to me at first. The resulting fascicle illustration gave that intermediate step a clear structural purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the constructions connect cellular mechanisms to larger-scale anatomy; the fibre-to-tendon force path and opposing elbow actions were particularly useful.
